scenes.title: The Problem with Traditional Access
scenes.narration: Many applications expose ports on origin servers, creating attack surfaces. Hackers scan for open ports, and if they find one, they can exploit vulnerabilities. This leaves your infrastructure at risk.

scenes.title: What Is a Zero-Trust Tunnel?
scenes.narration: A zero-trust tunnel creates an encrypted pathway between a client and a server without exposing the server’s ports. Instead of opening ports on the origin host, the tunnel brokers connections securely.

scenes.title: How the Tunnel Works
scenes.narration: The client connects to a relay server, which then forwards traffic to the origin host over a secure channel. The origin host never needs to expose its ports directly to the internet.

scenes.title: Benefits of Zero-Trust Tunnels
scenes.narration: Zero-trust tunnels reduce attack surfaces by eliminating exposed ports. They also enforce strict identity verification, ensuring only authorized users and devices can access resources.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.narration: Zero-trust tunnels improve security by removing exposed ports and enforcing strict access controls. This approach minimizes risk while maintaining secure, reliable connections.
